question: Should Microsoft Teams permanently support legacy root bot identity fields alongside `accounts.<id>`, with named accounts inheriting selected shared root settings?
rationale: Implementation quality cannot decide the long-term public config, inheritance, setup, and upgrade contract; that commitment requires an explicit Teams/config owner decision.

options.title: Sponsor the hybrid contract
options.body: Approve legacy root compatibility plus named accounts, document precise inheritance rules, and reopen or refresh this PR for landing.

options.title: Require accounts-only canonical config
options.body: Use a doctor migration for shipped root-level Teams identity fields and keep runtime configuration on one canonical account shape.

options.title: Do not add Teams multi-account support
options.body: Close the implementation direction and leave the canonical issue declined with the supported single-bot alternative.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the hybrid contract
recommendation.body: Approve legacy root compatibility plus named accounts, document precise inheritance rules, and reopen or refresh this PR for landing.
